sentences.text: 1  BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE 1.

The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (herein after referred to as PFA Act), alleging that the accused have violated the provisions of the PFA Act and Rules.

2. Initially, after conclusion of the trial, the accused persons namely Sh. B.B Garg, Sh. Ashok Bansal,
Sh. Ram Swaroop, Sh. J.S Rathore, Sh. Vinay Bagga and M/s Delhi Milk Scheme were convicted by the then, Ld. ACMM vide order dated 09.01.2019 under section 16(1)(a) of the PFA act read with section 7 of the PFA act and were accordingly sentenced.
3. The accused namely Ram Swaroop had challenged the order before the appellate court.

The Ld.
ASJ-04 had set aside the order of conviction and sentence vide order dated 09.01.2023 and remanded back the case with the following observations:
"Matter remanded back the Trial Court to proceed with the issue afresh, giving reasoning on the same i.e. whether the nomination form of the accused, only for the purposes of distribution, would still make him liable for prosecution and ABHISHEK by ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR

4. Accordingly, arguments were heard afresh at length on behalf of the accused Ram Swaroop and the department.
Furthermore, none of the parties requested or filed any application for adducing any additional evidence.

5. During the course of arguments, the accused did not dispute the proceedings conducted by the department regarding the lifting of the sample or the report of the food analyst finding the milk sample not conforming to the standards prescribed under the PFA Act and rules.
The accused Ram Swaroop had argued primarily with respect to his role in the commission of the crime.

He had stated that he could not have made liable on account of the nomination in his favour, which extended to the distribution activities whereas the sample was lifted from a different unit in the establishment,
where the accused had no role to play.
Thus, filing of the complaint against him was not proper on account of the limited nomination.
Thus, the quality control of the milk and its processing was not within the domain of his area of operation which extended to distribution.
Accordingly, accused prayed that he is liable to be acquitted in the present case.
6. On the other hand, Ld. SPP contended that the nomination form cannot restrict the liability of the accused.
Once, he was nominated, the accused being the in charge, can be held liable and responsible for ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR

8. It is the case of the complainant that on 06.08.2003 at about 10.00 am, the Food Inspector (herein after referred to as FI) Sh. R.K. Garg was found conducting the business of the said food article at the time of sampling.
9.

Further, the sample consisted 3 x 500ml sealed polythene packets 'Pasteurized Full Cream Milk',
having identical label declaration.

The sample was taken under the supervision/direction of Sh. S.K.
Nanda, LHA, after proper homogenization i.e by cutting the polythene packets and pouring the contents in a clean and dry patila and re-pouring the milk with the help of other clean and dry Patila.
10. Then, the Food Inspector divided the sample into three equal parts by putting them in three separate clean and dry bottles.
Further, 40 drops of formalin were added in each sample bottle.

sentences.text: Considering the defense raised by accused Ram Swaroop and the arguments presented, the pivotal question to address is whether Ram Swaroop can be held accountable for the offense.

This revolves around the fact that his nomination pertained solely ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR Date:

20. In this case, the FI had written a letter dated 26.09.2003(Ex. PW1/G) to Dr. P.K Vats, LHA,
department of PFA, seeking nomination details of the firm M/s Delhi Milk Scheme, Shadipur, West Patel Nagar, Delhi.
The LHA provided the information vide communication dated 16.10.2003 which is Ex. PW3/E.
Perusal of the communication reveals that accused Ram Swaroop was acknowledged as a nominee to the extent of his operation, which was mentioned as Manager (distribution).
The copy of the nomination form in favour of the accused was brought on record as Ex. PW3/D4.

Therefore, it is abundantly clear that accused was nominated to the extent of his area of operation i.e Distribution.
21.
At this point, it is deemed necessary to refer to Section 17 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration (PFA) Act and specifically to the explanation appended to clause (2) of the section.

Section 17 of the act read as follows:
17. Offences by companies.

-- (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company-- (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereinafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated,

Page No. 8 of 11 of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:
Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.

(2) Any company may, by order in writing, authorise any of its directors or managers (such manager being employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity) to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the commission by the company or any offence under this Act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority, in such form and in such manner as may be Delhi Administration vs B.B Garg Etc on 3 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9796682/
5 prescribed, that it has nominated such director or manager as the person responsible,
along with the written consent of such director or manager for being so nominated.

Explanation.--Where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, different persons may be nominated under this sub-section in relation to different establishments or branches or units and the person nominated in relation to any establishment, branch or unit shall be deemed to be the person responsible in respect of such establishment, branch or unit.

(3) The person nominated under sub-section (2) shall, until-- (i) further notice cancelling such nomination is received from the company by the Local (Health)
Authority; or (ii) he ceases to be a director or, as the case may be, manager of the company; or (iii) he makes a request in writing to the Local (Health) Authority, under intimation to the company,
to cancel the nomination [which request shall be complied with by the Local (Health) Authority.]
whichever is the earliest, continue to be the person responsible:
Provided that where such person ceases to be a director or, as the case may be,
manager of the company, he shall intimate the fact of such cesser to the Local (Health) Authority: Provided further that where such person makes a request under clause (iii), the Local (Health) Authority shall not cancel such nomination with effect from a date earlier than the date on which the request is made.

sentences.text: 22. With respect to the issue in hand, the explanation attached to section 17(2) of the PFA act is squarely applicable.

The accused in question was specifically responsible for overseeing the distribution area in the capacity of a manager, as confirmed by the nomination form, which explicitly acknowledges his area of operation as distribution.
Consequently, the quality control of the milk did not fall within his scope of responsibility, and he cannot be held accountable for it.
Various aspects, including quality processing, were managed by different individuals.
The nomination form brought on record clearly establishes the fact that accused was nominated to be responsible for the distribution activities.
Hence, it is established that the accused Ram Swaroop cannot be held responsible for the commission of the offense under Section 16 of the PFA Act.
His role did not involve ABHISHEK KUMAR KUMAR

24. Accused is directed to furnish personal bonds U/s 437A Cr.PC in the sum of Rs.10,000/-.
